check: No can-level quest-item drop is overridden by the generator that spawns it
passes when: zero overridden drops. `CSetDestroyedScriptActionAction` in a generator's `After Action` **replaces** the can's `Destroyed Script Action`, so a drop written only on the can is dead code -- this is how the Lava Troll Hide was unobtainable from 0.10.0

check: Every `=CSomething` names a class the engine registers
passes when: zero unknown classes. Checked against the C-prefixed strings in `Lionheart.exe` plus every class vanilla's data uses. An invented class is a hard CTD -- *"Invalid class type"* -- and `CIsQuestStatusCompletedAction` in the Grand Inquisitor's tree shipped in **0.13.0 and survived 27 tagged releases** before a player walked into it

check: No exit this mod makes reachable leaves the player inside a non-interactive sequence
passes when: zero hangs. Scoped to trees where **every** exit vanilla could reach ends the sequence, and only to exits vanilla could not already enter, so inherited shapes stay quiet. **Blind spot: "exit" means reply-reachable**, so a node a map opens directly is invisible -- grep the maps before satisfying this by adding actions to a node

check: A field with an empty value is not followed by a brace block
passes when: zero orphan blocks. 0.60.5 shipped a Crossroads crash every other gate passed

check: No value is itself a `Key=Value` assignment, and no interaction specifier is installed on the entity that is dying
passes when: zero. Both shipped: 0.71.10's builder wrote `Else=<tab>Dialog Tree File=...`, and a specifier added inside a destroyed script can only run once the entity is dead

check: **No node that hands out an item is reachable with no gate crossed while other replies to it are gated**
passes when: zero repeatable grants. Found in play in 0.83.3: Brendan's Serpent's Bile had six gated doors and one open one, so it could be taken every conversation. The naive form of this check -- *are all incoming replies gated* -- reports four more trees and all four are false positives, because a gate at a branch entrance with ungated replies inside it is the correct and ordinary pattern. So it walks from the entry points following only ungated replies

step: **Negative.** Equip a cloak
expect: Still the shield slot, as 0.83.0 set it, and still stacking with body armour. Nothing about the item was edited, only its art

step: Buy or find a **Scroll of Healing**. Take damage to roughly half health and read it
expect: **24-28 points plus 10% of your maximum health**, in one jump. At 100 max HP that is about 36

step: Read a Scroll of Healing at **full** health
expect: Nothing is consumed into nothing: the absolute-maximum message, same as a potion. The cap is `1.5 x maxHP - current`, so a full-health read has no headroom

step: Check its price and its drop grade in a shop
expect: **50 gold**, and it now appears in scroll loot at all. It was graded `1 Common` and absent from every generator, so that grade had never been exercised

step: **The row that proves the repair.** On one character, read a Scroll of Healing and drink an **Extra Healing potion** at the same max HP, noting both numbers
expect: The scroll heals **more** (24-28 + 10% against 18-22 + 10%). Before this it healed *less* (12-14 + 5%) while costing 50 against the potion's 22. If the scroll still heals less, the retune did not take and every other row here still passes

step: **The row that proves the chain.** Read a **Scroll of Mending** at low health and watch the health bar for twenty seconds
expect: **Four separate jumps** of 9-11 plus 3% of max HP, five seconds apart, starting immediately. Total about 40 + 12%. **One jump means the delay chain broke** and only the first tick fired, which SD6 and SD7 would not catch

step: Read a Scroll of Mending, then **keep fighting** through the twenty seconds
expect: The ticks keep arriving while you swing. This is the case the item exists for, and the one an instant potion cannot cover

step: Read a Scroll of Mending at **full** health, then take a hit after ten seconds
expect: The early ticks heal nothing and are **not wasted**: the cap is re-checked per tick, so the ticks after the hit still heal. No absolute-maximum message, by design -- four of them would be spam

step: **Die** during a Mending chain, or read it and then let a companion die mid-chain
expect: No crash and no healing of a corpse. Each tick is wrapped in `CIsAliveAction`, the guard `Wound Constrictor` uses

step: **The risk row.** Read a Scroll of Mending, then **change map** before the twenty seconds are up
expect: Unknown and untested: nothing in the game runs a delay chain from an item across a transition. Losing the remaining ticks is acceptable; a crash or a stuck effect is not. `Wound Constrictor` proves a delayed heal works from an item, not that it survives a map change

step: With a companion beside you, read a **Scroll of Mass Healing**
expect: **Both** of you heal 16-20 plus 8% of max HP. Radius 200, categories `Player,Player Friend`. It used to heal the identical amount to its own potion at 75 against 30

step: With a companion beside you, read a **Scroll of Renewal**
expect: Both of you heal **four times**, five seconds apart, 7-9 plus 2.5% each. An ally who walks into range after the first pulse is picked up by a later one, because each pulse re-reads who is nearby

step: **Negative, and the one that matters most.** Open the **herbalist's** shop at every stock tier and look for any scroll
expect: **There is none.** The herbalist sells potions, including Fixt's Great, Superior and Supreme Healing. If a scroll appears there, the picker edit leaked into the potion pool and the whole "magic vendors only" split is gone

step: Open **Weng Choi's** shop, the **Weird woman** in Hamlet Burned or the Witch Interior, or the **Rogue Inquisitor** on the Plains, and restock a few times
expect: Healing scrolls turn up. They stock the scroll pool, where Healing is now 22.1% of rolls. Before this the pool's most frequent entry was a Very Rare ward, so scrolls effectively never appeared

step: **Negative.** Buy or find each of the five ward scrolls -- Acid, Cold, Electrical, Fire Protection, Strength
expect: Unchanged in every respect: 40 resistance, their own durations, Very Rare and Unique, prices 125 and 350. Only the healing entries were touched

step: Play a **Demokin with Vampiric Fury** and read each of the four scrolls
expect: Every heal is **halved** -- 12-14 + 5% for Healing, 8-10 + 4% for Mass Healing, 4-6 + 1.5% per Mending tick, 4-5 + 1.25% per Renewal pulse. Every healing item in the game carries this branch and all four mirror it

step: Compare a **Scroll of Mending** (110) against a **Superior Healing potion** (150) at around 100 max HP
expect: Mending totals a little more, about 52 against 48, and takes twenty seconds to deliver it. That is the whole trade the scroll line is built on, and the reason the total is allowed to exceed an instant potion: no tick overheals

step: *(re-walk, 0.85.1's fix)* Set a companion to **Only fight back**, then let something hit **them** rather than you
expect: They swing back at what hit them. The forced target decays on their next pick, several times a second, so a burst then a pause is a pass; standing still and taking it is not

expect: They open fire **before** you are on them. Their radius went 550 to 850 against a standoff of 350, so they no longer acquire you and then walk 200 units closer before shooting

step: Fight the zombies in the Dream Djinni Map
expect: Same, and for the same reason: they count as ranged because they **throw chunks**, `Minimum Attack Distance=350`

step: **Negative, and the point of the row.** Fight the Terrors in Inquisition Pit3, the Lava Troll, or the Slave Pits melee
expect: A little more room before they commit, and **no more than that**. Confirmed in play: *"it doesn't feel vastly different, that's probably ok"*. If it reads as a difficulty drop, that is the risk this release carries and the reason to revert it

step: **Negative, the sweep that was reverted.** Commit a crime in the Gate, Port or Temple District; talk to Cedric; enter Shylocke's shop
expect: The guards react as before and every conversation opens as before. The first sweep caught the **Guard Reserves**, which are the crime system, plus `Cedric Talks to Player`, `check if player attack overrided` and `Start Here`, which are dialogue triggers. None of them is touched

step: Talk to a companion
say: Let's talk about how you fight.
expect: A second screen, *"How should they handle a fight?"*, offering **Only fight back**, **Fight as you see fit** and **Never mind**

step: **The row that proves the release.** Set *Only fight back*, then attack something yourself and leave them out of it
say: Only fight back.
expect: They **do not join in**. Confirmed in play: *"fang didn't participate in the wolves i was fighting"*

step: With that set, let something attack **them**
expect: They fight back, and go for whoever struck them. Confirmed in play: *"but fought back when attacked by another"*. Blanking `Valid Targets` alone would not do this -- pacification stops a companion seeing any target and only `Target shooter if hit` gets round it, so a melee attacker would be ignored entirely

step: **The defect FB3 hid.** After they have fought back, wait, then attack something else yourself and leave them out of it
expect: They stand down again and stay out of it. The first cut took their filter back and **never gave it up** -- the save showed `Valid Targets=Enemy` with the stance still reading 2, so the menu promised *"Do not start anything"* and after one blow they started things for the rest of the game. They now stand down 8 seconds after the last blow

step: Set *Only fight back*, then change your mind mid-fight
say: Fight as you see fit.
expect: They resume picking their own targets at once. The stand-down re-checks the stance before firing, so a late timer cannot un-do an order you have just given

step: Set a stance on one companion while travelling with two
expect: Only that one changes. The stance is held **on the companion**, one variable per instance, not fifteen player-scoped flags

step: Set *Only fight back*, save, reload
expect: It survives. Read it from the save as `Game Scripting Variables/Fixt Companion Stance=2`

step: **Regression.** Release a companion, and ask one how they are holding up
say: Release Companion
expect: 0.84.0's replies are untouched: the report still prints four lines and releasing still prints *"A companion has left your party"*

step: **Negative.** Check the attributes window
expect: `Fixt Companion Stance` does not appear. `Display In Attributes Window=0`, cloned from `Fixt Companion Fang`

step: Recruit each of the fourteen companions in turn and set a stance
expect: All fourteen obey. Six of them have cans that are **not** named after them -- Bishop Diego is `Diego`, Goblin Girl is `Mongol Vendor Village`, Darsh is `Inquisitor Darsch`, the Golem is `Wargolem Deactivated`, Grace is `Grace OMalley`, Cortes is `Cortez` -- and matching on scripting names alone missed every one

step: **Negative, the shared cans.** Fight a Mongol vendor-village goblin or a deactivated war golem that is **not** your companion
expect: They behave exactly as before. Two companion cans are shared with non-companions, and the hook does nothing unless `Fixt Companion Stance` is 2, which a non-companion never has

step: **Negative, the one that could break the game.** Fight Cervantes or Cortes as enemies, and watch for whatever their own damaged action does
expect: It still fires. Four of the fifteen cans already had something in that slot and were **wrapped**, not overwritten -- their `CRandomAction` and `CMultipleActionsAction` survive beside the new call

step: **The documented limit.** On a save where a companion was recruited **before** installing, set *Only fight back* and let something attack them
say: Only fight back.
expect: They hold their fire as told but **do not answer the attacker**. The hook lives in their can and a can edit reaches only creatures spawned after install. Release and re-recruit them, or set *fight as you see fit*

step: FB13, then release and re-recruit them and repeat
expect: `FB3` now passes for them

step: **The filter repair.** In Clan of the Hand A, Cave 3, the Slave Pits, Hamlet Exterior, Clan of the Skull B, Hamlet Burned, the Troll Pit, Inquisition Chambers2 or the Port District, stand a companion nearer an enemy than yourself
expect: That enemy can now attack the companion. **35 pickers** that allowed `Player` alone were widened to `Player,Player Friend`, which is what 547 other pickers in the game already allow

step: **Negative, the bosses.** Fight the Snakebreed Boss, the Assassin Master in the Slave Pits or the Burial Chamber, the Bird Man King, the Juanita shakedown Thug Boss or Aka Manah
expect: They still focus **you**. Nine boss pickers were left `Player`-only deliberately. Also unchanged: the chickens, the tortured prisoners, the Surrey merchant, the cloned guards, Joan of Arc, the Knight of Saladin, and the **Lost Knight**, who is a recruitable companion

step: Click a companion to open the order menu
say: How are you holding up?
expect: The conversation closes and the combat log carries **one line from each group**: how hurt, `Experience: level N`, `Health at full strength: X to Y`, a best-weapon line, `Fighting skill: A to B`. Five lines, no duplicates within a group

step: HV1 at full health
expect: `Not a scratch on me.` and nothing else from the health group

step: **PASSED.** Open the order menu to sync the label, then heal the companion past 75% and open it again
expect: `Fang (Injured)` and then plain `Fang`. Confirmed in play: *"the injured status was there and then got removed after healing"*. **`CSetCharacterDisplayNameAction` is repeatable** -- it fired twice on one entity in both directions, which no vanilla use does; all six rename the player once inside a conversation

step: Drive the same companion below 40%, then below 15%
expect: `(Badly Injured)` then `(Near Death)`. Healing back up walks the same three states in reverse

step: On a save where companions joined **before** this release, open the order menu once
expect: The watcher arms from that conversation. No re-recruiting, no new game

step: Hover **Fernand** while he is hurt
expect: `Fernand Desoto (Injured)`. His scripting name is `Distressed Sailor` and only the display name changes, so the label must read the name his dialogue uses. If his hover read something else before, this release changes it

step: **Negative, the one that could break the game.** After a companion has been renamed, level up and watch for the growth balloon
expect: It still appears over them. The balloon anchors on `Name of Position=Fang` and every quest lookup uses `Name To Check For=Fang`; only the *display* name is rewritten, so nothing that resolves a companion by name may break

step: **Regression.** Release a companion
say: Release Companion
expect: They leave and `A companion has left your party` prints, exactly as before. The reply gained one canned action and lost nothing

step: Open the menu on one companion, then immediately on a second
say: How are you holding up?
expect: The second report describes the **second** companion. `Character to get attributes from=$Trigger` must resolve to whoever you clicked

step: Report a companion's level against your own
expect: Plausible, and not stuck at `level 1` for someone who has travelled with you for ten. `CVariableCharacterLevel` has never been read off a non-player character in this project

step: Hover **Cervantes before recruiting him** while he is hurt
expect: He may show a band. Not a defect: the fifteen names are companion scripting names and the watcher arms on any of them present in the map

step: Open the menu twice on the same companion and release and re-recruit between
expect: One watcher, not two. The per-companion `Fixt Companion Health Watch <name>` guard blocks the second install

step: **The hole HV3 first fell into.** Arm the watcher while the companion is *already* below 75%, then hover without healing them
expect: The label is correct **immediately**, from the ungated current-band sync. Without that sync nothing appears: `CAIHealthPercentThresholdTrigger` is edge-triggered, so a watcher armed on a wounded companion records their percent as its baseline and fires nothing until they heal past a threshold and come back down. Fang sat at `Previous Health Percent=57.0512` with `Is Valid=1`, a correct six-threshold watcher, and no band at all

step: Open the order menu twice at different health levels
expect: The label resyncs each time. The sync is deliberately **ungated** so a missed crossing cannot leave a stale label forever

step: **The shipped defect this playtest found.** Recruit a companion and **never open the order menu**. Level up
expect: The growth balloon still appears. Before this release both installers were invoked from *one* place -- a reply in `Generic Companion Dialog` -- so a player who never clicked a companion got **no growth for the whole game**. A save with Fang in the party for several levels had `Fixt Companion Growth Watch`, `CXRPGAITriggerWhenLevelUp`, `Fixt Companion Health Watch` and `CAIHealthPercentThresholdTrigger` all at zero

step: HV15 on each of the fourteen companions
expect: All fourteen `Fixt Companion Joined/<name>.can` files now call both installers, outside their own `Fixt Companion <name> == 0` test so a re-recruit arms too. Both installers are internally guarded, so arming twice is a no-op

step: **Regression on the growth watcher's target.** Level up with a companion present
expect: The companion gains the modifiers. The growth installer's `CAddAIAction` now targets `Player1` instead of `$Instigator`, because `$Instigator` is only the player when the can is called from a dialogue reply -- pinning it is what lets the Joined cans call it at all. `CXRPGAITriggerWhenLevelUp` must sit on the **player**

step: Check the attributes window
expect: None of the fifteen `Fixt Companion Health Watch <name>` variables appear. They carry `Display In Attributes Window=0`, cloned from `Fixt Companion Fang`

section: The first enemy healer in the game
step: **Run this before the rest.** Start a new game and play any ordinary fight -- thugs in the Port District will do. Also skim your character sheet's skill list, and fold in `EH3` while you are there
expect: **You are looking for nothing to happen.** Port thugs are not the Priest family, so no new behaviour should appear; this only confirms that adding a 93rd `.Skill` to a 92-skill game broke nothing. **Checked 2026-10-10 and the risk is narrower than this row used to claim:** `Skill Values` is keyed by **full path name** with **no `Item Count`** (184 entries of `Skills/<path>=v,min,max`), so there is no positional index and **adding a skill cannot shift anything**. The only live question is whether a name-lookup miss returns 0 or errors. Fail looks like an enemy standing inert or using a visibly wrong attack, a blank or duplicated entry in the skill list, or a crash on entering combat or opening the skill tree -- **not** odd numbers. If it fails, the fallback needs no new skill at all: `CGiveHealthToCharacterAction` fired from a can makes an enemy heal itself. **PASSED 2026-10-10** -- Port District thugs fought normally on a fresh game. The 93rd `.Skill` breaks nothing, so **0.33.0 and 0.34.0 are no longer at risk of wholesale removal** and the name-keyed `Skill Values` reading is confirmed in play. Note this clears the *structural* gate only: the healing feature itself is still unproven, and `EH1` (act 6, a Priest and soldiers together) remains the row it exists for

section: The twenty-one meshes, and the pools that deliver them
where: A **Better or Special** magic **Composite** Long Bow

pass: Same mesh, `BowSpecial`. The Composite's own base art is the best bow in the game, so its copies name `BowSpecial` at both tiers rather than downgrading it to `BowBetter`. **The grade is the whole row.** A Composite carrying a Basic addition such as `of Dodging` has already been held in play and looked right, but Basic additions name no mesh, so that proves only that the Composite's pool delivers. Confirm the enchantment is Better or Special before reading anything into the model
